name: Primalist
body:
As wilderness warriors, primalists rely on their nature magic and spirit guide to survive the outback’s greatest challenges. As the spirit guide bonds with its host, the primalist evolves, relying on instincts and frenzied attacks to survive.

Role: When frenzying, primalists make formidable combatants, and when using their nature-based magic, they provide supplemental healing and protective buffs for wilderness excursions.

Alignment: Any

Hit Dice: d8

Alternate Class: Hunter

Starting Wealth: 4d6 x 10 gp (average 140 gp).

Class Skills

The primalist’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Handle Animal (Wis), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Perception (Wis), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Spellcraft (Int), Stealth (Dex), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks Per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Class Features

The following are class features of the primalist.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

A primalist is proficient with blowguns, slings, Stone Age weapons (atlatl, great terbutje, mere club, taiaha, tepoztopilli, terbutje, and wahaika), and the weapons listed in both the bows and tribal fighter weapon groups.

Spellcasting

A primalist casts divine spells drawn from the Hunter spell list. The primalist’s base daily spell allotment is given on Table 1: Primalist. In addition, a primalist receives bonus spells per day if they have a high Wisdom score. To learn or cast a spell, a primalist must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell’s level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a primalist’s spell is 10 + the spell’s level + the primalist’s Wisdom modifier.

A primalist doesn’t need to prepare their spells in advance. They can cast any spell they know at any time, assuming they have not used up their spells per day for that spell level. See Table 2: Primalist Spells Known to determine how many spells of each level a primalist knows. At 5th level and every three levels thereafter, a primalist can choose to learn a new spell in place of one they already know. In effect, the primalist loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged.

A primalist may swap only a single spell in any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that they gain new spells known for the level.

Orisons: A primalist learns a number of orisons, or 0-level spells, as noted on the table Spells Known. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they do not consume any slots and may be used again.

Font (Ex)

A primalist draws their power to cast magic from the land, sky, or water.

At 1st level, a primalist chooses their font which provides two known spells per spell level. These spells do not count against the primalist’s maximum number of known spells. A primalist never needs material components when casting a spell gained from their font (or font focus).

Land Font

You can manipulate earth to carve passages through cave walls, create difficult terrain, and batter opponents with stones.

Spells: 1st–mudball, stone shield, 2nd–stone call, stone discus, 3rd-earth tremor, raging rubble, 4th–calcific touch, earth glide, 5th– hungry earthmc , transmute rock to mud, 6th–dust form, elemental body lll (earth only).

Sky Font

Your magic reflects the nature of celestial bodies, circadian rhythms, avians, and aerial weapons.

Spells: 1st–commune with birds, gravity bow, 2nd-aggressive thundercloud, blinding ray, 3rd–daylight, deeper darkness, 4th–cloud shape, wandering star motes, 5th–air walk, communal, control winds, 6th–cloak of dreams, elemental body lll (air only).

Water Font

Your connection to water as the fount of life gives you abundant healing power.

Spells: 1st–cure light wounds, lesser restoration, 2nd–cure moderate wounds, soothing word, 3rd–cure serious wounds, soothing mud, 4th–cure critical wounds, restoration, 5th–breath of life, cleanse.

At 3rd level, a primalist’s source of magical power becomes even more specialized. The primalist chooses one of the two font focuses associated with their chosen font. They gain the spell listed for each level as an additional spell known that does not count against their maximum total of known spells.

Also at 3rd level, the primalist gains 1 bonus spell slot per day. The bonus spell slot can only be used to cast a font or font focus spell. For example, a 4th level primalist can cast 1st and 2nd level spells.

They gain 1 bonus spell slot which they can use to cast either one 1st level font/font focus spell or one 2nd level font/font focus spell. The primalist can choose a different font/font focus spell when they use this ability each day.

Land Font

Flora Focus-You are a plant whisperer.

Spells: 1st–goodberry, 2nd-climbing beanstalk, 3rd–burst of nettles, 4th-explosion of rot , 5th–plant shape I, 6th–transport via plants.

Mining Focus-You can excavate dirt, tunnel through stone, and manipulate metal.

Spells: 1st–expeditious excavation, 2nd-molten orb, 3rd– spiked pit, 4th–rusting grasp, 5th–passwall, 6th–wall of iron.

Sky Font

Combustion Focus-You draw upon the oxygen in air to create magnificent fire effects with your magic.

Spells: 1st–produce flame, 2nd–flame blade, 3rd–fireball, 4th–flame strike, 5th–fire snake, 6th–fire seeds.

Lightning Focus-Your affinity for the heavens manifests as the ability to call lightning and create electrical effects to protect yourself.

Spells: 1st–shock shield, 2nd-elemental touch (electricity), 3rd–call lightning, 4th–ball lightning, 5th–call lightning storm, 6th–chain lightning.

Water Font

Depths Focus-The ocean influences your magic, granting you the power to swim, breathe water, and create cold effects.

Spells: 1st-wave shield, 2nd–water walk, communal, 3rd–life bubble, 4th–ride the waves, 5th–cone of cold, 6th–cold ice strike.

Mutability Focus-You can change water’s state from liquid to boiling to solid ice.

Spells: 1st-snowball, 2nd-flurry of snowballs, 3rd–hydraulic torrent, 4th–geyser, 5th–icy prison, 6th–fluid form.

Instinctive Defense (Ex)

A primalist wears hides and pelts like a second skin and reacts to danger with the wisdom of a wild animal. At 1st level, a primalist does not incur an armor check penalty when wearing light armor, with the exception of chain shirts. (A primalist wearing a chain shirt incurs its armor check penalty as normal.) Furthermore, when unarmored, not using a shield, unencumbered, and conscious, a primalist adds their Wisdom bonus (if positive) to their AC and CMD. If the primalist is wearing armor or using a shield, they instead add 1/2 their Wisdom bonus to their AC and CMD.

In addition, the primalist gains a +1 bonus to their AC and CMD at 4th level.

This bonus increases by 1 for every 4 primalist levels thereafter (up to a maximum of +5 at 20th level).

These bonuses to AC apply even against touch attacks and when the primalist is flat-footed.

The primalist loses these bonuses when they are immobilized or helpless. These bonuses do not stack with the monk AC bonus class feature.

Natural Vitality (Su)

A primalist can channel the power of nature to stimulate a body’s natural ability to heal itself. As primalists grow in power, they gain immunity against various ailments.

At 1st level, as a standard action, the primalist can touch a living creature (constructs and undead are unaffected) to grant it fast healing equal to 1/2 their primalist level (minimum 1) for 1 minute.

Additionally, while a creature is under the effects of natural vitality, it receives a bonus on all saving throw rolls against poison and disease equal to the primalist’s Wisdom modifier. A primalist can activate natural vitality on themselves with a swift action instead of a standard action. A primalist can use this ability a number of times per day equal to 1/2 their primalist level (minimum 1) + their Wisdom modifier (if positive).

At 7th level, the primalist gains immunity to disease (natural and magical).

At 13th level, the primalist gains immunity to poison.

At 19th level, the primalist gains immunity to the exhausted, nauseated, sickened, and staggered conditions.

Primal Reserve (Ex)

At 1st level, primalists gain a primal reserve that augments their instincts and enhances their physical prowess, helping them to succeed at difficult tasks. The number of points in a primalist’s reserve is equal to 3 + 1/2 their primalist level (minimum 1) + their Wisdom modifier (if positive). The total number of points in the reserve replenishes after resting for 8 hours, although these hours need not be consecutive. As long as a primalist has at least 1 point in their reserve, they gain a bonus equal to 1/2 their primalist level (minimum 1) on Knowledge (Nature) and Survival skill checks.

A primalist can expend points from their primal reserve to gain the following abilities: Instinctive Response: When a primalist must make a saving throw, ability check, or skill check, they can use a free action (or an immediate action for a saving throw roll) to expend 1 primal point from their reserve to add 1d4 to the result of the roll. At 18th level, the primalist adds 1d6 to the result of the roll instead. The primalist can choose to expend the point after determining if their initial roll is successful or not.

Wild Sprint: As a swift action, a primalist can expend 1 primal point to sprint. Wild sprint grants a +10 foot bonus to the primalist’s land speed and lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1 + the primalist’s Constitution modifier (if positive). This bonus increases to +20 feet at 9th level and +30 feet at 17th level.

Wild Stride (Ex)

Over time, a primalist masters all of nature’s terrains, traveling through them with ease. At 1st level, a primalist can move through any sort of undergrowth (such as natural thorns, briars, overgrown areas, and similar terrain) at their normal speed, and without taking damage or suffering any other impairment.

At 6th level, a primalist gains a 30 foot climb speed and a 30 foot swim speed.

At 14th level, whenever a primalist encounters magically manipulated terrain or vegetation that would impede movement (for example entangle), the primalist automatically treats the terrain as normal and can move through it freely without hindrance.

Frenzy (Ex)

At 2nd level, when taking the full-attack action, a primalist can frenzy.

When frenzying, the primalist makes an additional attack at their highest base attack bonus. (This additional attack stacks with haste effects.)

Spirit Guide (Su)

A primalist forges a permanent bond with an ancestral spirit that guides the primalist along their path in life, alerting them to danger, protecting them from harm, and helping them to survive in the wilderness. A spirit guide is a formless entity that merges with the primalist. It occupies the same space as the primalist, is invisible, and is completely indistinguishable from the primalist. A spirit guide can’t be killed or affected as a separate entity.

When a primalist dies, the spirit guide returns to the Astral Plane, and the primalist loses all benefits conferred by their spirit guide until they merge with a new one. A raised or reincarnated primalist can merge with a new spirit guide 24 hours after returning to life.

There are three types of spirit guides: warrior, witch doctor, and soothsayer. At 2nd level, a primalist chooses one of the three types of spirit guides to bond with.

This choice is permanent and can’t be changed. As the primalist grows in power, they are eventually able to bond with additional spirit guides. The benefits from a primalist’s spirit guide are as follows: Warrior: You are bonded with a protective spirit that bolsters your ability to defeat your enemies and overcome threats to your survival. At 2nd level, you gain the bonus feat Endurance or Weapon Focus (your choice; you do not need to meet the prerequisite). If you already have both of these feats, you can select Weapon Focus again for a different weapon.

In addition, choose a single weapon with which you are proficient. You gain a +1 bonus on damage rolls made with the selected weapon. At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, this bonus to damage increases by +1 to a maximum of +5 at 20th level.

Witch Doctor: You are bonded with a healing spirit that bolsters your ability to recover from wounds that endanger your life. At 2nd level, you gain the bonus feat Diehard or Toughness (your choice) and add +1 round to the number of rounds your natural vitality class feature lasts when you use it on yourself. If you already have both of these feats, every day at dawn, you gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your level which disappear the following day at dawn if they haven’t already been depleted.

At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, you add +1 round to the number of rounds your natural vitality class feature lasts when you use it on yourself (to a maximum of +5 additional rounds at 20th level).

Soothsayer: You are bonded with a sighted spirit that lets you see moments into the future to mount your best defense against those who wish you harm. At 2nd level, you gain the bonus feat Dodge or Improved Initiative (your choice) and a +1 bonus on Perception and Sense Motive checks. If you already have both of these feats, you gain a +1 insight bonus to your AC.

At 5th level, and every five levels thereafter, the bonuses to Perception and Sense Motive increase by +1 to a maximum of +5 at 20th level.

At 9th level, a primalist chooses a second spirit guide with which to bond and gains the 2nd level benefit for that spirit. At 17th level, a primalist bonds with the third spirit guide and gains the 2nd level benefit for that spirit. A primalist never gains additional benefits or bonuses, beyond those granted at 2nd level, from their second and third spirit guides.

Clan Weapon (Ex)

A primalist selects one Stone Age or tribal weapon (from their weapon proficiencies class feature) to be their clan weapon. The primalist is especially skilled in the chosen weapon’s use. At 4th level, a primalist gains a +1 insight bonus on attack rolls made with their clan weapon. At 8th level, and every four levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +1, to a maximum of +5 at 20th level.

Greater Frenzy (Ex)

At 11th level, when primalists make a frenzied attack, they gain two extra attacks instead of one.

Lethal Frenzy (Ex)

At 20th level, when making a successful bonus attack granted by their frenzy class feature, a primalist adds their Wisdom modifier (if positive) to the damage rolls.

Furthermore, all potential critical hits made with a bonus attack granted by their frenzy class feature are automatically confirmed.
